observations:
Torah 74 (LM2) is an incomplete, fragmentary teaching. The Rebbe explicitly stopped mid-discourse in paragraph 4 ('וּפָסַק בְּאֶמְצַע הָעִנְיָן וְלֹא גִּלָּה יוֹתֵר') and did not finish the final paragraph ('וְלֹא סִיֵּם'). The extant text consists of only 5 short paragraphs, and the bechina content is entirely captured in the three packages identified.

All bechina statements in the text are already mapped to nodes in the dataset:
1. שפתותיו = פסח (Package 3) — directly from the verse
2. שושנה = אסתר (Package 2) — from Zohar and Arizal
3. מרדכי = מר דרור = חרות = חרות של פסח (Package 1) — from Hullin 139b etymology

The only candidate for additional bechina language is the phrase 'בִּתְחִלָּה הוּא בְּחִינַת פּוּר' in paragraph 2, which links פורים to the lot (פּוּר). However this is an etymological note (Purim is named for the pur-lottery) rather than a substantive thematic cluster with 3+ concepts. It does not constitute an independent domain that requires a new package.

The teaching does not develop any evil/negative conceptual domain — no forces of opposition, no klipah figures, no anti-concepts. The good/evil mirror structure that characterizes complete Torahs is absent here, consistent with the truncated nature of the text.

Conclusion: With 3 packages covering all 7 bechina nodes from 5 bechina edges, the existing package structure is complete and exhaustive for the content that exists in this Torah. No additional packages are warranted.
